anya (product): Quick sync — sprint-zero scenarios for Private Delivery (VPC / on‑prem). We need to pick the top 3 scope options to drive Q3 launch criteria. Focus: customer-managed networking, upgrade paths (zero-downtime if possible), and packaging options (online installer, airgap, operator). Please drop constraints, blockers, and minimal acceptance criteria.

Tom (eng-runtime): +1. From runtime side, hard constraints: GPU kernel selection and sequence-length tradeoffs will affect the smallest viable image. We should define a target max seq len and a quantization baseline.

Lucy (field): Customers care about preserving existing egress IPs, predictable peering, and audit trails. Many ask for a documented rollback window and a staging cutover plan. Also: one customer explicitly requires KMS integration and no outbound control plane.

Dan (infra): Networking note: "customer-managed networking" means we can't assume NAT vs. public IPs. Installer needs flags for `--assume-nat` and `--egress-ip=<ip>` and a preflight that verifies BGP/peering routes. Offline mode must include an image checksum manifest and local bundle verification.

anya (product): Good. Can we sketch 3 concrete scope options so we can prioritize? Minimal / Recommended / Enterprise. Keep each 2–3 bullet acceptance criteria.

Tom (eng-runtime): Minimal: basic operator install, provides a default nat-relay, docs for port requirements. Acceptance: install completes in <15min in our lab env, model endpoints respond at expected latency (p50 < 120ms for small models), and automated health checks surface KV cache warming.

Tom (eng-runtime): Recommended: support customer-managed egress IP + DNS-preserve migrator. Acceptance: preflight checks for egress IP, operator supports `--pin-egress`, and rolling upgrade with no more than 5s additional p95 latency during handoff.

Dan (infra): Enterprise: airgapped bundle + KMS/HSM integration + explicit onprem control plane option. Acceptance: offline installer with signed bundles, KMS via customer gateway (test vector), and network policy verifier that passes real customer topologies in lab (examples: mTLS-only, private peering).

Lucy (field): Add launch gates: must have at least 2 field pilot customers for Recommended, and 1 enterprise pilot for Enterprise. Also need docs & runbook for rollback and an SLO for upgrade success rate (>= 95% across pilot fleet).

anya (product): Perfect. Quick risk calls — what are the top 3 engineering risks that could delay Q3?

Tom (eng-runtime): 1) Kernel/quantization regressions when switching to smaller images. 2) Live upgrade ordering across heterogeneous GPUs (must avoid KV cache invalidation). 3) Operator lifecycle edgecases with mixed-version clusters.

Dan (infra): Ops risk: customers with strict egress constraints that block telemetry/health checks. We need a clear plan: local health sinks + optional aggregated logs upload when allowed.

Lucy (field): Sales risk: pilots taking >12 weeks to onboard because of netops involvement. Mitigation: provide a prepackaged network checklist and a small network white‑glove offer from Solutions.

anya (product): Can someone draft a minimal preflight checklist we can ship to Solutions/SEs? Keep it short.

Tom (eng-runtime): Draft checklist:```
- Verify control-plane reachability (or opt-out for airgap)
- Confirm egress IPs / NAT behavior
- Validate required ports (operator, grpc, metrics)
- KMS endpoint reachability if requested
- Disk space >= 50GB on model nodes
- GPU drivers >= supported version
```

Dan (infra): Add: `- If airgapped: provide signed bundle + bootstrap token` and `- Confirm time sync (NTP)`

Lucy (field): I'll add a customer-facing one-pager: onboarding roles (netops, app owner, se) + estimated calendar: 2 weeks prework, 1 week install, 2–6 weeks validation.

anya (product): Next steps: 1) Ship this thread as a short decision memo. 2) Announce prioritization rubric in next product triage. 3) Assign owners for each scope bucket. Owners: Tom = Minimal/Recommended runtime; Dan = Enterprise infra/airgap; Lucy = field pilots & docs.

infra-bot: CI status: nightly-private-installer build 2026-03-22 — failed on `bundle-sign` step. Link: https://ci.redwood/ins/priv-installer/20260322 :warning:

Tom (eng-runtime): Noted. That failing step blocks Enterprise demo. I'll pick it up tomorrow.

Lucy (field): I'll pause enterprise sales asks until we have the signed-bundle flow green.

anya (product): Thanks all. I'll post the decision memo and add these owners to the triage board. :thumbsup:
